all_passages.content: My husband handles the business accounts, but household savings I manage. I keep some in post office savings — very safe. And we have a lot of gold. My mother-in-law's jewellery, some coins we bought for the children's future. On festivals we always buy some.
No, what is that? Is it like an online thing?
But where is the gold? I can't see it? What if the company closes? This is risky no?
I don't know these names. For me gold means I can touch it, keep it in my house or locker. Online gold feels like it's not real.
What does that mean? Like interest on gold?
That would be good. But why is someone giving me interest on my gold? Who is using my gold?
Jewellers I understand. But I would want to know — is my gold actually there? Can I take it back as physical gold if I want?
That makes me feel better. But delivery charges will be there? And making charges?
CoinDCX — I've never heard this name. What kind of company is this? If it's a new company, no. If it's like a bank or government, then okay.
SEBI I've heard. But it's not a bank. Can the bank offer this? HDFC or SBI?
Then I'd want to know — has anyone I know used it? If my neighbour or someone in my kitty party has used it and found it good, then I'd consider. Otherwise I won't risk it.
Route 1 — 'Your gold, always yours.' This I understand. Route 2 with 'earns more gold every year' — I like the idea but it sounds too good. I don't fully believe it.

This needs to come through someone I trust — a bank, a post office, or someone in my community. Marketing in apps won't work for people like me. Also, show me a clear certificate that my gold exists. If I get a paper saying 'Sunita Patil owns 10 grams stored in XYZ vault,' then I'll feel comfortable.
